name: Extra Eyes
tagline: Turn a spare phone into a camera that rings another phone.
description: Point one Android phone at a door or room and mark the area you care about. When someone comes in, your other phone rings. Video stays on your own Wi-Fi, encrypted, with no account, cloud or server.

platforms.note: Install this on the camera phone and the watcher phone. Photo and Video need Android 10 or later.
Optional. Installing on a watch needs Wireless debugging and adb on a computer.

features.title: Mark what matters
features.text: Draw an area with up to 12 dots, a line, or watch the whole view, so people passing outside don't ring it.

features.title: Person detection
features.text: On-device AI rings only for a person in the area. Turn it off to ring on any movement.

features.title: Alarm sounds
features.text: Thirteen alarm, gentle and funny sounds. It rings once per visit, even on silent.

features.title: Live video
features.text: Watch from another phone or a watch. Pick the ultrawide, wide or tele lens on the camera.

features.title: Photo and video
features.text: Save pictures and clips to the gallery, from either phone or from the watch.

features.title: Battery warnings
features.text: See the camera's battery, with a warning at 30% and again at 20%.

features.title: Wear OS watch
features.text: Video, alarms and captures on your wrist, with or without a watcher phone.

features.title: Share the app
features.text: Send the app straight to another phone from the main screen.

setup: Install the app on two phones and join the same Wi-Fi.
On the camera phone, tap Pair phones, then Show code.
On the watcher phone, tap Pair phones, then Scan code.
On the camera phone, choose Camera and drag the red dots around the door.
To add a watch, open Extra Eyes on it, then tap Connect watch on a phone and scan the watch's code.
limits: Both phones must be on the same Wi-Fi. Guest networks often block them from reaching each other.
It's an alert for when you step away, not a security system. Nothing is recorded unless you press Photo or Video.
With the app closed, a watch gets alarms only from the phone it's paired with, within Bluetooth range.
Android will warn that the app comes from an unknown source.
